jobs.title: Senior Bio Information Analyst - Ecological Data & Significant Natural Areas
jobs.description:
Lead the management and analysis of ecological and Significant Natural Area datasets
Use spatial data and remote sensing to support evidence-based environmental decision-making
Influence how ecological information supports planning, policy and environmental protection outcomes

He angitūtanga: The opportunity

Auckland Council's Environmental Services department has an opportunity for a Senior Bio Information Analyst to join our Bio Information Team.

This role focuses on the management, analysis and continuous improvement of ecological information that supports biodiversity protection, environmental planning and Significant Natural Area (SNA) programmes across Tāmaki Makaurau.

Working alongside ecologists, planners and technical specialists, you'll help ensure environmental data is robust, accessible and fit for purpose. You'll take a leading role in maintaining key ecological datasets, providing specialist spatial analysis and developing innovative approaches to environmental data capture, classification and reporting.

This is an opportunity to influence how ecological evidence is used to inform environmental policy, planning decisions and long-term biodiversity outcomes for Auckland.

Please note:
The official title for this position is Senior Bio Information Analyst. We've included Ecological Data & Significant Natural Areas in the advertised title to reflect the primary focus areas of this vacancy.

Day-to-day you could expect to:

Lead the management and maintenance of SNA, ecosystem and ecological datasets.
Undertake spatial data reviews and quality assurance to support environmental decision-making.
Develop and improve ecological data capture, classification and analysis methodologies.
Apply remote sensing and image analysis techniques to support ecological assessment and monitoring.
Deliver specialist GIS, mapping and reporting services for environmental programmes and projects.
Mentor others in spatial data methodologies

He kōrero mōu: About you

You'll bring a strong understanding of environmental information management and enjoy turning complex ecological data into meaningful insights that support real-world environmental outcomes.

You are naturally curious, analytical and collaborative, with the confidence to provide expert technical advice while helping others build their capability.

Our must-haves:

A relevant Bachelor’s degree in an environmental discipline, natural sciences or computer science, together with 7+ years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of natural sciences, ideally New Zealand ecology, and experience working with environmental information.
Proven experience developing and implementing information, database, geospatial or data-support solutions.
Advanced capability in ESRI ArcGIS/spatial mapping and/or database design and management, with strong Microsoft Office skills and experience using relevant ecological analysis software.
A full NZ driver’s licence, along with the communication, initiative, relationship-building and resilience to operate confidently in a complex, collaborative environment.

Nice to haves:

A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
Experience with ecological surveys and assessing the significance of natural areas.
Knowledge of SQL database design and functionality in an environmental management context.
Experience specifically across biodiversity, biosecurity or geological information.
Experience mentoring other analysts or leading technical work, projects or information initiatives.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is passionate about the role environmental information plays in protecting and managing Auckland's natural environment. You’ll ideally have experience working with SNA and ecosystem datasets, regional or local plan mapping, remote sensing and image analysis, and an understanding of the RMA and planning system transformation will be highly valued.

You’ll also bring an appreciation of Te Ao Māori and tikanga, and a willingness to continue developing your confidence and capability in te reo Māori and our Treaty responsiveness journey.

ACZ Laboratories’ reputation as a leader in the environmental testing industry is a direct result of the quality of our employees. We believe in hiring highly motivated professionals with dedication to data quality, personal integrity, and a strong work ethic.

Auckland Council's Environmental Services department has an opportunity for a Senior Bio Information Analyst to join our Bio Information Team.

This role focuses on the management, analysis and continuous improvement of ecological information that supports biodiversity protection, environmental planning and Significant Natural Area (SNA) programmes across Tāmaki Makaurau.

Working alongside ecologists, planners and technical specialists, you'll help ensure environmental data is robust, accessible and fit for purpose. You'll take a leading role in maintaining key ecological datasets, providing specialist spatial analysis and developing innovative approaches to environmental data capture, classification and reporting.

This is an opportunity to influence how ecological evidence is used to inform environmental policy, planning decisions and long-term biodiversity outcomes for Auckland.

Please note:
The official title for this position is Senior Bio Information Analyst. We've included Ecological Data & Significant Natural Areas in the advertised title to reflect the primary focus areas of this vacancy.

Day-to-day you could expect to:

Lead the management and maintenance of SNA, ecosystem and ecological datasets.
Undertake spatial data reviews and quality assurance to support environmental decision-making.
Develop and improve ecological data capture, classification and analysis methodologies.
Apply remote sensing and image analysis techniques to support ecological assessment and monitoring.
Deliver specialist GIS, mapping and reporting services for environmental programmes and projects.
Mentor others in spatial data methodologies

He kōrero mōu: About you

You'll bring a strong understanding of environmental information management and enjoy turning complex ecological data into meaningful insights that support real-world environmental outcomes.

You are naturally curious, analytical and collaborative, with the confidence to provide expert technical advice while helping others build their capability.

Our must-haves:

A relevant Bachelor’s degree in an environmental discipline, natural sciences or computer science, together with 7+ years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of natural sciences, ideally New Zealand ecology, and experience working with environmental information.
Proven experience developing and implementing information, database, geospatial or data-support solutions.
Advanced capability in ESRI ArcGIS/spatial mapping and/or database design and management, with strong Microsoft Office skills and experience using relevant ecological analysis software.
A full NZ driver’s licence, along with the communication, initiative, relationship-building and resilience to operate confidently in a complex, collaborative environment.

Nice to haves:

A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
Experience with ecological surveys and assessing the significance of natural areas.
Knowledge of SQL database design and functionality in an environmental management context.
Experience specifically across biodiversity, biosecurity or geological information.
Experience mentoring other analysts or leading technical work, projects or information initiatives.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is passionate about the role environmental information plays in protecting and managing Auckland's natural environment. You’ll ideally have experience working with SNA and ecosystem datasets, regional or local plan mapping, remote sensing and image analysis, and an understanding of the RMA and planning system transformation will be highly valued.

Hard contents
Clothing and textiles
Electronics
Appliances
Artwork and decorative items
Household goods
Specialty and high-value contents

Hand cleaning

Deodorization
HEPA cleaning
Smoke and soot removal
Textile restoration
Specialty vendor restoration

Provide documentation necessary to support the services performed.

Help resolve customer or insurance questions before they delay the project.

Prepare or assist in preparing contents restoration estimates using industry-standard estimating practices and software.

Identify missed billable services and legitimate supplemental items.
Monitor labor, materials, subcontractors, storage and project costs.
Help ensure projects are properly documented, invoiced and financially closed.
Maintain awareness of project gross margin and department profitability.
Help management identify opportunities to improve productivity and profitability.

Team Leadership

Lead, schedule and coordinate Contents Technicians.
Establish daily production priorities.
Train employees in proper packing, inventory, cleaning, handling and documentation procedures.
Maintain high standards for productivity, workmanship and professionalism.
Perform quality-control inspections throughout each project.
Hold team members accountable for documentation, organization and customer service.
Assist with recruiting, onboarding and developing additional contents personnel as the division grows.

Ensure customer belongings remain properly labeled and separated.
Maintain organized vaulting, shelving and storage systems.
Coordinate incoming pack-outs and outgoing pack-backs.
Maintain appropriate cleaning equipment, materials and supplies.
Help improve warehouse workflows as contents volume increases.

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidate will have previous experience in property restoration, contents restoration or insurance-related property claims.

We are particularly interested in candidates with experience managing contents following:

Fire and smoke losses
Water damage
Sewage or contaminated losses
Mold remediation
Large residential losses
Commercial property losses

2+ years of restoration or contents restoration experience.
Previous project management, crew leadership or supervisory experience.
Experience with insurance restoration claims.
Strong understanding of pack-out, inventory, cleaning, storage and pack-back procedures.
Comfortable communicating with homeowners and insurance professionals.
Strong organizational and documentation skills.
Ability to manage several projects simultaneously.

Comfortable learning and working with digital inventory, photography and project-management systems.

Takes ownership without needing constant direction.
